title: Text Emphasis & Formatting ✍️
description: Master bold, italic, highlight, and more – plus the difference between semantic and presentational tags.

slides.title: Semantic vs Presentational 🤓
slides.content:
# Meaning or Just Looks?

HTML offers two types of formatting tags:
- **Semantic** tags convey **meaning** (important for accessibility & SEO).
- **Presentational** tags just change **visual style** (better to use CSS instead).

When possible, use semantic tags. They help screen readers and search engines understand the importance of your text.

slides.title: Bold: `<strong>` vs `<b>` 💪
slides.content:
# Emphasis vs Attention - `` – **strong importance**. Screen readers will emphasise this text. Use for warnings, key terms. - `` – simply **bold text** with no extra meaning. Use for product names, lead sentence, or keywords (but not to convey importance). Example: ```html

Warning: This product may cause drowsiness.

The XYZ 2000 is the latest model.

```

quizData.question: Which tag should you use to mark truly important text that a screen reader should stress?
quizData.explanation: <strong> indicates strong importance; <b> is purely visual.

slides.title: Italic: `<em>` vs `<i>` ✨
slides.content:
# Stress vs Alternate Voice - `` – **emphasised** text (stressed pronunciation). Use to change the meaning of a sentence. - `` – **idiomatic** text (alternate voice, technical terms, thoughts). ```html

I really need that report by noon.

The term status quo is often misused.

```

slides.title: Emphasis in Context
slides.codeSnippet:
I didn't say she stole your money.

I didn't say she stole your money? (Implies someone else's.)

slides.title: Other Handy Text Tags 🧰
slides.content:
# Highlight, Small, Delete, Insert, etc.

- `<mark>` – highlights text (like a marker pen).
- `<small>` – fine print, disclaimers, side comments.
- `<del>` – deleted text (strikethrough).
- `<ins>` – inserted text (underlined).
- `<sub>` – subscript (H₂O).
- `<sup>` – superscript (x²).

All are **semantic** – they add meaning beyond just look.

slides.title: Text Formatting Showcase
slides.content: A paragraph that uses several tags at once:
slides.codeSnippet: Sale! The Pro 3000 is now $199 $99. Remember: H2O is essential and E = mc2. Terms apply.

quizData.question: <i> and <em> are identical in meaning and can be used interchangeably.
quizData.explanation: <i> is presentational (italic); <em> is semantic (stress). Use <em> when you want to emphasise meaning.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use CSS for Visual Italics

If you just need italic for style (like a book title), use `<cite>` (semantic) and style it with CSS, or `<i>` for a purely visual italic. Prefer semantic tags and style later.
